subject: Embeddings integration: batching / normalization / migration - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@acme.com>, Elena Morris <elena.morris@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Embeddings integration - post-call recap & next steps

Hi Samir / Elena —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: \

Summary of what ACME is trying to solve:
- Migrate semantic search embeddings from current provider (Pinecone + older model) to Redwood’s managed embeddings + vector DB
- Improve reranking quality for product search with a lightweight reranker on top of kNN
- Reduce per-op cost and latency with batching and normalization pipeline

Key technical notes from call:
- Desired vector dimension target: 1536 for parity with the new open model you want to evaluate. You mentioned some legacy vectors at 768 that we may need to up-convert or reindex.
- Query throughput: ~250 qps peak, typical 60 qps.
- Max acceptable p95 latency for search: 120ms (end-to-end).

Proposed next steps (action items):
1) Engineering sync (Dylan, Samir) — deep-dive on SDK auth and routing, and validation of existing vector schema. Dylan to propose a short test harness. (Target: Thu 23 Jul)
2) Migration plan — we’ll provide a recommended re-index flow for transforming 768 -> 1536 vectors, and measure quality delta. Marissa to send spec + sample vectors.
3) Batching & normalization recommendations — default batch size suggestions, L2 vs cosine normalization guidance, and a small benchmark harness to measure latency/cost tradeoffs.
4) Access & credentials — please share a sandbox dataset or sample CSV (anonymized) and confirm the HubSpot deal id; we’ll send a scoped API key for Redwood Private test env.

Attachments: embeddings_spec_v1.pdf (high-level migration plan), sample_vectors.csv (small export you can use with the harness).

If that matches your expectation, I’ll loop in Dylan and Dev (solutions eng + infra) and propose times for the engineering sync.

Thanks,

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@acme.com>

Cc: Elena Morris <elena.morris@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Embeddings integration - post-call recap & next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is perfect. Quick clarifications:

- We definitely want to target 1536 going forward. The 768 vectors are from a 2023 model; we can re-run offline, but would like an approach for incremental migration (keep search online while re-indexing).
- For reranking: we plan to run a lightweight transformer-based reranker (on CPU or small GPU) that takes top-50 candidates from the vector DB and scores them. We’d like an example of integrating an embeddings+reranker pipeline using Redwood’s SDK.
- On auth: we prefer scoped API keys per environment. We can consume short-lived tokens if Redwood supports them; otherwise scoped static keys are fine for the PoC.

We’ll upload a sanitized sample CSV to the Drive link you provided by EOD. Can Dylan propose 30–45 minute slots tomorrow? Elena will join the engineering sync.

—Samir
Engineering Manager, Search
ACME Corp

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.inference>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 23 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Embeddings integration - post-call recap & next steps

Samir — thanks, looking forward to the sync. A few quick technical bullets so the meeting is productive: \

1) SDK + auth: Redwood SDK supports API keys and short-lived JWTs via our token-exchange endpoint. For the PoC I’ll create a scoped API key limited to "embeddings:read,embeddings:write,search:query" and a test dataset. We can show an example in Node + Python.

2) Batching: for 1536-d vectors we typically see best throughput at batch sizes between 64–256 vectors depending on GPU and padding; for CPU vectorization we recommend 16–64. I’ll include a small benchmark.

3) Normalization & similarity: we recommend L2-normalized vectors with cosine similarity at query time for cross-model parity. If you must keep legacy 768 vectors online during migration, we suggest running hybrid search:
   - Keep legacy index for 768 vectors for immediate traffic
   - Re-index documents to 1536 in a new index; at query time, run both indexes and merge top-k with lightweight reranker scores

4) Reranker integration: we’ll provide a sample flow where Redwood returns top-100 candidates; the reranker (on your side) scores top-50 and returns final ranking. We can demo tool-calling/structured output by returning candidate metadata alongside vectors (doc_id, score, snippet) so your reranker can use context.

5) Migration caveats: up-converting 768->1536 by padding or projection is lossy; best results come from re-encoding text with the new model. We’ll measure recall and precision on a held-out eval set.

Attached I’m dropping a short script example and a config snippet (I’ll paste during the call). Proposed times: Thu 23 Jul 2:00pm PT or Fri 24 Jul 10:00am PT. Which works?

Thanks,
Dylan
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.inference
